passages.text: These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant He had made with them at Horeb.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD gave commands to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to make a covenant with the Israelites.
This happened in the land of Moab.
This covenant is in addition to another covenant.
The LORD had already made a covenant with the Israelites at Horeb.
passages.original: אֵלֶּה֩ דִבְרֵ֨י הַבְּרִ֜ית אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה לִכְרֹ֛ת אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב מִלְּבַ֣ד הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁר־ כָּרַ֥ת אִתָּ֖ם בְּחֹרֵֽב׃פ

passages.text: Moses summoned all Israel and proclaimed to them, “You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to all his land.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses called all the people of Israel together.
Moses spoke to them.
He said, “You have seen everything the LORD did in Egypt.
You saw these things with your own eyes.
The LORD acted in Egypt against Pharaoh.
The LORD acted against all Pharaoh’s officials.
The LORD acted against all the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה לְעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְפַרְעֹ֥ה וּלְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֖יו וּלְכָל־ אַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You saw with your own eyes the great trials, and those miraculous signs and wonders.
passages.sermon:
You saw these things with your own eyes.
You saw great trials.
You saw great signs.
You saw great wonders.
God did these things before you.
God showed His power to you.
passages.original: הַמַּסּוֹת֙ הַגְּדֹלֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָא֖וּ עֵינֶ֑יךָ הָאֹתֹ֧ת וְהַמֹּפְתִ֛ים הַגְּדֹלִ֖ים הָהֵֽם׃

passages.text: Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to all Israel.
He reminded them of what the LORD did in Egypt.
He said the LORD acted against Pharaoh, his officials, and all his land.
Moses said, "Until today, the LORD has not given you understanding."
He said, "The LORD has not given you eyes that truly see."
He said, "The LORD has not given you ears that truly hear."
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ נָתַן֩ יְהוָ֨ה לָכֶ֥ם לֵב֙ לָדַ֔עַת וְעֵינַ֥יִם לִרְא֖וֹת וְאָזְנַ֣יִם לִשְׁמֹ֑עַ עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For forty years I led you in the wilderness, yet your clothes and sandals did not wear out.
passages.sermon: God led the Israelites for forty years in the wilderness.\r\nDuring those forty years, their clothes did not wear out.\r\nTheir sandals did not wear out on their feet.
passages.original: וָאוֹלֵ֥ךְ אֶתְכֶ֛ם אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר לֹֽא־ בָל֤וּ שַׂלְמֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וְנַֽעַלְךָ֥ לֹֽא־ בָלְתָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל רַגְלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites in the wilderness for forty years.
During this time, the Israelites did not eat bread.
They did not drink wine.
They did not drink strong drink.
God did this for a reason.
God wanted the Israelites to know something important.
God wanted them to know that He is the LORD their God.
passages.original: לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אֲכַלְתֶּ֔ם וְיַ֥יִן וְשֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א שְׁתִיתֶ֑ם לְמַ֙עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When you reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us in battle, but we defeated them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites came to this place.
Sihon was king of Heshbon.
Og was king of Bashan.
Sihon and Og came out to fight us.
They came out for battle against us.
We defeated Sihon and Og.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־ הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֣א סִיחֹ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ־ חֶ֠שְׁבּוֹן וְע֨וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַבָּשָׁ֧ן לִקְרָאתֵ֛נוּ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה וַנַּכֵּֽם׃

passages.text: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites took the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan.
They gave this land as an inheritance.
The Reubenites received part of the land.
The Gadites received part of the land.
The half-tribe of Manasseh received part of the land.
passages.original: וַנִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ אַרְצָ֔ם וַנִּתְּנָ֣הּ לְנַחֲלָ֔ה לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֖י וְלַגָּדִ֑י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשִּֽׁי׃

passages.text: So keep and follow the words of this covenant, that you may prosper in all you do.
passages.sermon:
God gave you a covenant.
This covenant has words and commands.
You must keep these words.
You must do what they say.
If you obey, you will have wisdom.
You will succeed in everything you do.
passages.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֗ם אֶת־ דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֔ילוּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃פ

passages.text: All of you are standing today before the LORD your God—you leaders of tribes, elders, officials, and all the men of Israel, your children and wives, and the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water— so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, which He is making with you today, and into His oath, and so that He may establish you today as His people, and He may be your God as He promised you and as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
passages.sermon:
All of you are standing here today.
You stand before the LORD your God.
You are the leaders of your tribes.
You are the elders and officials.
You are all the men of Israel.
You are your children and your wives.
You are the foreigners living among you.
Some of you cut wood in your camp.
Some of you draw water in your camp.
You are all here for a purpose.
You are here to enter into a covenant with the LORD your God.
The LORD your God is making this covenant with you today.
He is also making an oath with you today.
He does this to make you His people today.
He wants to be your God.
He promised this to you.
He swore this to your fathers.
He made this promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
passages.original: אַתֶּ֨ם נִצָּבִ֤ים הַיּוֹם֙ כֻּלְּכֶ֔ם לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם רָאשֵׁיכֶ֣ם שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֗ם זִקְנֵיכֶם֙ וְשֹׁ֣טְרֵיכֶ֔ם כֹּ֖ל אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ טַפְּכֶ֣ם נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם וְגֵ֣רְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֶ֑יךָ מֵחֹטֵ֣ב עֵצֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד שֹׁאֵ֥ב מֵימֶֽיךָ׃ לְעָבְרְךָ֗ בִּבְרִ֛ית יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּבְאָלָת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כֹּרֵ֥ת עִמְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃ לְמַ֣עַן הָקִֽים־ אֹתְךָ֩ הַיּ֨וֹם׀ ל֜וֹ לְעָ֗ם וְה֤וּא יִֽהְיֶה־ לְּךָ֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־ לָ֑ךְ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁבַּע֙ לַאֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: I am making this covenant and this oath not only with you, but also with those who are standing here with us today in the presence of the LORD our God, as well as with those who are not here today.
passages.sermon:
God is making a covenant and an oath today.
He is not making this covenant and oath only with you who are here now.
He is also making it with those who are standing here with us today before the LORD our God.
He is also making it with those who are not here with us today.
passages.original: וְלֹ֥א אִתְּכֶ֖ם לְבַדְּכֶ֑ם אָנֹכִ֗י כֹּרֵת֙ אֶת־ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶת־ הָאָלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃ כִּי֩ אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֶשְׁנ֜וֹ פֹּ֗ה עִמָּ֙נוּ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד הַיּ֔וֹם לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְאֵ֨ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ פֹּ֖ה עִמָּ֥נוּ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the nations on the way here.
passages.sermon:
You are the people of Israel.
You know what happened in the past.
We lived in the land of Egypt.
We left Egypt together.
We traveled through many nations on our way here.
You saw these things yourselves.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַתֶּ֣ם יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יָשַׁ֖בְנוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָבַ֛רְנוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַרְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: You saw the abominations and idols among them made of wood and stone, of silver and gold.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites saw the idols of the nations.
These idols were abominations.
The idols were made of wood and stone.
Some idols were made of silver and gold.
The nations kept these idols with them.
passages.original: וַתִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־ שִׁקּ֣וּצֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת גִּלֻּלֵיהֶ֑ם עֵ֣ץ וָאֶ֔בֶן כֶּ֥סֶף וְזָהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִמָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Make sure there is no man or woman, clan or tribe among you today whose heart turns away from the LORD our God to go and worship the gods of those nations. Make sure there is no root among you that bears such poisonous and bitter fruit, because when such a person hears the words of this oath, he invokes a blessing on himself, saying, ‘I will have peace, even though I walk in the stubbornness of my own heart.’ This will bring disaster on the watered land as well as the dry.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
He warned them about turning away from Him.
He said, "Be careful that no one among you turns away from the LORD our God."
This includes any man, any woman, any family, or any tribe.
Do not let anyone choose to worship the gods of other nations.
Do not let anyone's heart turn away from God today.
Do not let there be a root among you that produces poisonous and bitter fruit.
This root means a person who brings harm and leads others astray.
If someone hears the words of this oath and blesses himself in his heart, he is in danger.
He may say, 'I will have peace.'
He may think, 'I can go my own way and follow my stubborn heart.'
He believes nothing bad will happen to him.
But this attitude brings disaster.
It brings harm to both the watered land and the dry land.
It brings trouble to everyone, not just to himself.
passages.original: פֶּן־ יֵ֣שׁ בָּ֠כֶם אִ֣ישׁ אוֹ־ אִשָּׁ֞ה א֧וֹ מִשְׁפָּחָ֣ה אוֹ־ שֵׁ֗בֶט אֲשֶׁר֩ לְבָב֨וֹ פֹנֶ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ לָלֶ֣כֶת לַעֲבֹ֔ד אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָהֵ֑ם פֶּן־ יֵ֣שׁ בָּכֶ֗ם שֹׁ֛רֶשׁ פֹּרֶ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְלַעֲנָֽה׃ וְהָיָ֡ה בְּשָׁמְעוֹ֩ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֨י הָֽאָלָ֜ה הַזֹּ֗את וְהִתְבָּרֵ֨ךְ בִּלְבָב֤וֹ לֵאמֹר֙ שָׁל֣וֹם יִֽהְיֶה־ לִּ֔י כִּ֛י בִּשְׁרִר֥וּת לִבִּ֖י אֵלֵ֑ךְ לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת הָרָוָ֖ה אֶת־ הַצְּמֵאָֽה׃

passages.text: The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, His anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will fall upon him. The LORD will blot out his name from under heaven and single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will not forgive this man.
The LORD will become very angry with him.
The LORD will be jealous against him.
Every curse written in this book will come upon him.
The LORD will erase his name from under heaven.
The LORD will set him apart for disaster.
The LORD will do this among all the tribes of Israel.
The LORD will bring on him all the curses of the covenant.
These curses are written in this Book of the Law.
passages.original: לֹא־ יֹאבֶ֣ה יְהוָה֮ סְלֹ֣חַֽ לוֹ֒ כִּ֣י אָ֠ז יֶעְשַׁ֨ן אַף־ יְהוָ֤ה וְקִנְאָתוֹ֙ בָּאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא וְרָ֤בְצָה בּוֹ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣אָלָ֔ה הַכְּתוּבָ֖ה בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה וּמָחָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ שְׁמ֔וֹ מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ וְהִבְדִּיל֤וֹ יְהוָה֙ לְרָעָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּכֹל֙ אָל֣וֹת הַבְּרִ֔ית הַכְּתוּבָ֕ה בְּסֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then the generation to come—your sons who follow you and the foreigner who comes from a distant land—will see the plagues of the land and the sicknesses the LORD has inflicted on it.
passages.sermon:
Your sons will come after you.
They are the next generation.
A foreigner may also come.
He may come from a distant land.
They will see this land.
They will see the plagues on the land.
They will see the sicknesses in the land.
The LORD has brought these plagues and sicknesses on the land.
passages.original: וְאָמַ֞ר הַדּ֣וֹר הָֽאַחֲר֗וֹן בְּנֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָק֙וּמוּ֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵיכֶ֔ם וְהַ֨נָּכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖א מֵאֶ֣רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֑ה וְ֠רָאוּ אֶת־ מַכּ֞וֹת הָאָ֤רֶץ הַהִוא֙ וְאֶת־ תַּ֣חֲלֻאֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר־ חִלָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: All its soil will be a burning waste of sulfur and salt, unsown and unproductive, with no plant growing on it, just like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His fierce anger.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD punishes those who abandon His covenant.
He makes the land a burning waste.
The soil is covered with sulfur and salt.
No one sows seed in it.
Nothing grows in it.
No plant rises from the ground.
The land becomes like Sodom and Gomorrah.
The land becomes like Admah and Zeboiim.
The LORD destroyed these cities in His fierce anger.
The LORD overthrew them because of His wrath.
passages.original: גָּפְרִ֣ית וָמֶלַח֮ שְׂרֵפָ֣ה כָל־ אַרְצָהּ֒ לֹ֤א תִזָּרַע֙ וְלֹ֣א תַצְמִ֔חַ וְלֹֽא־ יַעֲלֶ֥ה בָ֖הּ כָּל־ עֵ֑שֶׂב כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת סְדֹ֤ם וַעֲמֹרָה֙ אַדְמָ֣ה וּצְבֹיִּים אֲשֶׁר֙ הָפַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאַפּ֖וֹ וּבַחֲמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So all the nations will ask, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?’
passages.sermon:
All the nations will see what happened to the land.
They will ask a question.
They will say, “Why did the LORD do this to this land?”
They will ask, “Why is the LORD so angry?”
passages.original: וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם עַל־ מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה כָּ֖כָה לָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את מֶ֥ה חֳרִ֛י הָאַ֥ף הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And the people will answer, ‘It is because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The people will answer.
They will say why this happened.
They will say the people abandoned the covenant.
The LORD made this covenant.
The LORD is the God of their fathers.
The LORD made the covenant with them.
He made it when He brought them out of Egypt.
passages.original: וְאָ֣מְר֔וּ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽזְב֔וּ אֶת־ בְּרִ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּרַ֣ת עִמָּ֔ם בְּהוֹצִיא֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: They went and served other gods, and they worshiped gods they had not known—gods that the LORD had not given to them.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel left the LORD their God.
They served other gods.
They worshiped these other gods.
They did not know these gods before.
The LORD had not given these gods to them.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיַּֽעַבְדוּ֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם אֱלֹהִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ יְדָע֔וּם וְלֹ֥א חָלַ֖ק לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against this land, and He brought upon it every curse written in this book.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD became very angry with the land of Israel.
The LORD’s anger burned because the people broke His covenant.
The LORD brought every curse on the land.
These curses are written in this book.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑וא לְהָבִ֤יא עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַקְּלָלָ֔ה הַכְּתוּבָ֖ה בַּסֵּ֥פֶר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: The LORD uprooted them from their land in His anger, rage, and great wrath, and He cast them into another land, where they are today.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD became very angry with the people.
He showed great wrath and fierce rage.
The LORD removed the people from their own land.
He uprooted them because of His anger.
The LORD sent them into another land.
They remain in that other land to this day.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּשֵׁ֤ם יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם בְּאַ֥ף וּבְחֵמָ֖ה וּבְקֶ֣צֶף גָּד֑וֹל וַיַּשְׁלִכֵ֛ם אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ אַחֶ֖רֶת כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
He knows all secret things.
Only God owns the hidden things.
He does not reveal everything to us.
God gives us some things openly.
The things God reveals belong to us.
They also belong to our children.
These revealed things belong to us and our children forever.
God reveals them for a reason.
We must do all the words of this law.
God wants us to obey His law.
We use what God reveals to follow His commands.
passages.original: הַ֨נִּסְתָּרֹ֔ת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהַנִּגְלֹ֞ת לָ֤ׄנׄוּׄ וּׄלְׄבָׄנֵׄ֙יׄנׄוּׄ֙ עַד־ עוֹלָ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת־ כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃ס
